Hinton.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Hinton calls follow the ground the town sits on: new River and Greenbrier River confluence at the city, steep forested slopes rising behind the terraced neighborhoods, Bluestone Lake country to the south. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

In fall and winter, squirrels and rodents push into warm attics across the county, and spring brings denning raccoons looking for chimneys and soffits to raise young. Hinton's historic districts hold rail-era brick and frame homes terraced up the hillside above the rivers. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.
